text: Sell SGLP.L immediately — it's down 99.2% from its high with a relative strength score of -98.9, meaning it's weaker than virtually every other stock out there, and this looks like a broken instrument you should exit completely.
Trim RGTI — you're down 21.7%, revenue is actually shrinking, it's 55% off its high, and it's the weakest of your quantum computing holdings, so reduce your exposure before further deterioration.
Trim LPTH to lock in some of that +50% gain — a PE of 131 with negative free cash flow and four consecutive earnings misses means the valuation has no fundamental support if sentiment shifts.
Trim SKYT into strength — a +67% gain at its 52-week high sounds great, but bearish MACD on an unprofitable company means this is the time to take some profit off the table, not add risk.
Add to META — at a PE of 17.5 with 22% revenue growth and strong free cash flow, this is arguably the best value in big tech right now and deserves a larger position.
Add to RTX — a quality defense name at a reasonable PE of 23.8 with positive free cash flow and a consistent earnings beat streak makes this a solid compounder to build into.
Add to LMT — Lockheed Martin's PE of 16.5 with 5.7% free cash flow yield is attractive for a blue-chip defense company, and defense spending tailwinds remain strong.
Add to MSFT — at a PE of 23.3 with nearly 15% revenue growth and a consistent earnings beat streak, Microsoft is a quality compounder trading at a reasonable price.
